advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the duplicated _load_access_check bootstrap with a call to the existing _lib_ops._engine_module('rebar_reconciler.access_check').
evidence: _lib_ops.py:141-153 `_engine_module` has an identical body and is already used at _lib_ops.py:340 to load `rebar_reconciler.access_check`
_lib_ops module-level imports (config, _engine, _errors) are Jira-free, so reusing it would not violate the doctor-stays-Jira-free contract
advisory.finding: _load_access_check duplicates the existing _lib_ops._engine_module bootstrap verbatim (same spec_from_file_location + submodule_search_locations + sys.modules insertion), instead of reusing it; the two loaders can drift.
advisory.suggested_fix: In audit_mapped_project_visibility, drop _load_access_check and do: `from rebar._lib_ops import _engine_module; access_check = access_check_mod or _engine_module('rebar_reconciler.access_check')`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Derive the projects.json/repo_root passed to the visibility check from the same tracker directory fsck audits, so a non-standard --tickets-tracker path is not silently read as an empty mapping.
evidence: access_check.py:377-381 `required = required_project_keys(...)`; `if not required: return ProjectVisibilityResult(status='ok')` — an empty mapping yields an 'ok' verdict with nothing checked
bridge_fsck.py:643-646 shows --tickets-tracker may be any explicit path, and the env/default paths only coincide with a '.tickets-tracker'-named dir
advisory.finding: The CLI passes tracker_path.parent as repo_root, but load_mapping/required_project_keys always rebuild '<repo_root>/.tickets-tracker/.bridge_state/projects.json'; when --tickets-tracker points at a directory not named '.tickets-tracker', .parent is not the repo root and the mapping is silently read from the wrong/absent path, yielding an empty required set and a false 'ok' advisory.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test injecting an access_check_mod (or probe) whose check_mapped_project_visibility raises, asserting verdict status='error'/reason='probe_error' and no propagation.
evidence: src/rebar/_engine_support/bridge_fsck_visibility.py:91: `except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — advisory diagnostic must never crash fsck`

ABSENCE: tests/scripts/bridge/test_bridge_fsck.py adds four visibility tests (missing / ok / skipped / cli-stderr) plus doctor; none inject a probe or access_check_mod whose check_mapped_project_visibility raises, so the error-swallowing contract is unexercised.
advisory.finding: The new probe-error swallowing path in audit_mapped_project_visibility (the `except Exception` branch returning status='error', reason='probe_error') has no test. The diff's docstring explicitly claims 'Any probe error is likewise swallowed into an advisory verdict', but no test injects a raising probe/access_check to force this branch, so a regression that let the exception propagate (crashing bridge fsck) would go undetected.
scenarios: A future change re-raises inside check_mapped_project_visibility, or the swallow is removed, hard-failing bridge fsck — no test catches it.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test passing access_check_mod with a check_mapped_project_visibility that raises RuntimeError, asserting the returned dict has status=='error' and reason=='probe_error'.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add tests asserting format_visibility_advisory output lines for at least the 'missing', 'ok', and 'skipped' verdicts (naming the missing keys in the 'missing' case).
evidence: src/rebar/_engine_support/bridge_fsck_visibility.py:118-121: the `missing` branch renders '  NOT visible to the bot: ' + missing keys and a 'required:'/'Fix projects.json' line
ABSENCE: no test in tests/scripts/bridge/test_bridge_fsck.py calls format_visibility_advisory; the only stderr check is a loose substring in the CLI test.
advisory.finding: format_visibility_advisory is untested. It has five status branches (ok / missing / skipped / transport_unavailable / else) that each shape distinct human-readable output, but no test asserts any of its returned lines. In particular the 'missing' branch — which renders the invisible keys, the entire point of the diagnostic — has its output completely unverified.
scenarios: A regression drops the missing-keys list or the fix hint from the advisory; the stdout JSON contract still passes and the loose stderr substring still matches, so nothing fails.
advisory.suggested_fix: Feed the verdicts returned by the existing missing/ok/skipped tests into format_visibility_advisory and assert the rendered lines contain the expected keys/status text.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Strengthen the CLI test to assert the stderr contains the skip verdict text (e.g. 'skipped' and 'credentials'), not just a header substring.
evidence: Diff: `assert "live" in captured.err.lower() or "visib" in captured.err.lower()`
src/rebar/_engine_support/bridge_fsck_visibility.py:114: header line 'Mapped-Project Live Visibility' always emitted first, so the substring matches on any verdict.
advisory.finding: The CLI integration test asserts too little on the advisory: `"live" in captured.err.lower() or "visib" in captured.err.lower()`. This matches the static header line '--- Mapped-Project Live Visibility (advisory) ---' regardless of the verdict, so it would still pass if the skip verdict were mis-rendered, empty, or replaced by an error — it does not verify the credential-absent skip path actually produced its skip line.
scenarios: The skip path stops emitting its 'skipped: no live Jira credentials' line but still prints the header; the assertion still passes.
advisory.suggested_fix: Assert `"skipped" in captured.err` and `"credentials" in captured.err.lower()` to pin the actual no-creds skip advisory.
